description: Run-time data providers and the forcing they give a Problem and its rhs_program (API_SPEC §5.8, "Forcing sets"; esm-libraries-spec §2.5.2). Each case builds the fixture with a set of providers and checks the program's forcing slots, its default forcing set, the program's right-hand side at the default state with that set, and the Problem's own right-hand side at its initial state. Every comparison is bitwise against the values below.

scope_excluded.python: No native program (API_SPEC §5.8): rhs_program raises compiler_unavailable.

provider: A provider entry is passed under `key` in the construction option `providers`. It delivers one field, keyed by `key`, whose value at time t is base + slope * t elementwise; `base` is nested row-major (outer list = first index) over `shape`, and a 0-d field is one number. `refresh_times` empty makes it a const provider; otherwise it is discrete with those refresh times. Julia: `provider_sample(p, t)` returns that field (a 0-d one as a one-element vector) and `provider_refresh_times(p)` the times. Rust: a `CadenceProvider` whose `materialize()` returns the field at `slope = 0` (const providers only), whose `refresh(t)` returns `Some` of the field at t, and whose `refresh_times()` returns the times.

checks.forcing_slots: forcing_slots(prog) equals forcing_slots: name, shape and kind, in this order
checks.default_forcing: each buffer of default_forcing_set(prog) / prog.default_forcing() equals default_forcing[slot], column-major, bitwise
checks.du_default: the program's right-hand side at default_state(prog), the default parameter vector, t = tspan[0] and the default forcing set equals du_default bitwise
checks.problem_du: the Problem's own right-hand side (Julia: prob.f!; Rust: debug_eval_rhs_into on the Problem's compiled model) at its initial state, its parameters and t = tspan[0] equals du_default bitwise

cases.note: The control: no data is supplied, so each declared default is the parameter's value.

Providers keyed by the parameters' qualified names, on a document with one model. Rust used to write their data under `Fed.s` next to the declared default under the bare compiled name `s`, so the Problem read the default and rhs_program's default set held either one, depending on map iteration order.

The same const providers keyed by the bare parameter names `E` and `s` (esm-spec §6.6.2). Julia's Problem used to read the declared default for the 0-d `s`: its build matched a bare const key to a shaped parameter only.

Discrete providers (a refresh time inside tspan) are sampled at construction, at sample_time, which defaults to tspan[0] = 0. Rust used to sample them first when a solve started, so the Problem's forcing and rhs_program's default set held the declared defaults. Julia's Problem used to read the 0-d `s` from its parameter vector, which held the declared default, rather than from the live buffer.
The same discrete providers sampled at an explicit sample_time = 0.25: each field is base + slope * 0.25.

The discrete providers of discrete_at_tspan_start keyed by the bare names `E` and `s`. Julia used to keep each live buffer under the caller's key, which the build never reads: both parameters kept their declared defaults in the Problem, and rhs_program's default set gained two extra slots, `E` and `s`.
